meta.title: Holding On Strong
meta.description: Still Holding On” — An anthem for those who keep going, even when the road won’t end.  Guided by a radio playing memory tunes, the traveler rides endless highways with dreams in his pocket, hope in his song, and scars on his soul. Faded photos, laughter turned to gold, truths whispered in stories — he’s tasted sorrow, savored sweetness, and crossed borders that carried his feet. He watches sunrises when sleep won’t come, chases daylight and truth in equal measure. And when night falls? He still whispers — no, he sings — like a vow: “I’m still holding on.”  This is a song about resilience. About motion as medicine. About carrying wishes and burdens in the same heartbeat. For anyone who’s ever kept driving… even when the road felt too long, the weight too heavy — but the belief? That never ran out.

metadata.prompt:
Ich steh total auf Pekingente

Strophe 1
Ich schlender durch die Straßen,
der Duft zieht mich magisch an,
ein kleines Himmelsfest aus Gewürzen,
das ich so sehr lieben kann.

Refrain
Oh, Pekingente, du machst mich verrückt,
mit deiner knusprigen Haut, so unverrückt.
Jeder Biss ein Traum, der mich entzückt –
ich steh total auf Pekingente!

Strophe 2
Die Sonne geht langsam unter,
doch mein Herz bleibt hell und weit,
in jedem saftigen Moment,
ist deine Köstlichkeit bereit.

Bridge
Mit jedem Kauen, jedem Lachen,
verschmilzt der Alltag in Magie,
ein Fest der Sinne, ohnegleichen,
du bist mein kulinarisches Genie!

Refrain
Oh, Pekingente, du machst mich verrückt,
mit deiner knusprigen Haut, so unverrückt.
Jeder Biss ein Traum, der mich entzückt –
ich steh total auf Pekingente!

Strophe 3
Ob im Restaurant oder zu Hause,
dein Geschmack verzaubert mich,
und wenn die Welt mal grau erscheint,
bringst du Farbe in mein Gesicht.

Outro
So sing ich dieses Lied der Freude,
für den Geschmack, der mich entführt,
denn in jeder knusprigen Erinnerung,
wird mir stets dein Zauber gespürt.

Oh, Pekingente,
du bist mein Traum, mein kulinarischer Stern,
für immer bleibst du in meinem Herzen,
unvergleichlich, köstlich und so fern!

The Velveteen Rabbit is a children's book by Margery Williams Bianco that was first published in 1922. It tells the story of a stuffed rabbit who wants to become real through the love of his owner, a young boy. Here is a brief summary of the plot:

- The rabbit is given to the boy as a Christmas present, but he is soon neglected and put in the toy box with the other toys.
- The rabbit learns from the Skin Horse, an old and wise toy, that toys can become real if they are loved by children for a long time.
- The rabbit becomes the boy's favorite toy and enjoys playing with him in the spring and summer.
- The rabbit meets some real rabbits who tell him that he is not a real rabbit because he cannot hop or run like they do.
- The boy gets sick with scarlet fever and the rabbit stays with him until he recovers.
- The doctor orders that all the boy's toys should be burned to prevent infection, including the rabbit.
- The rabbit cries a real tear and a fairy appears. She tells him that he has become real to the boy and she will make him real to everyone else.
- The fairy takes the rabbit to the forest where he meets other real rabbits and lives happily ever after.

The book is a classic of children's literature and has been adapted into many different forms, such as films, plays, musicals, and ballets. It explores themes such as love, imagination, reality, and identity. 🐇❤️

They said the world would hum in wires,  
Machines would croon the sweetest choirs,  
That metal hands and neon scenes  
Would play the chords and spin the themes.  

But baby, let me tell you true,  
The soul won’t dance to auto-tune.  
A ghost in circuits can’t improvise,  
A heart don’t beat in digitized skies.  

The future is acoustic, can’t you see?  
Brass will cry and bass runs free.  
Ivory whispers, cymbals sigh,  
A saxophone will kiss the sky.  
No click track, no cold refrain,  
Just rhythm breathing in the rain.  

They built their walls of ones and zeros,  
Called their silence brand-new heroes.  
But when the night falls soft and blue,  
It’s jazz that tells the story true.  

The future is acoustic, mark my words,  
A wooden soul beats wired worlds.  
Electric dreams may come and go,  
But swing will never lose its glow.  

Let the cities blink and whir,  
Let the satellites purr…  
In the cracks, sun and moonlight slips,  
You’ll hear a sax, a bass, a kiss…  
The future is acoustic, love,  
And jazz will rise above.

metadata.prompt:
1 tablespoon of olive oil
1 tablespoon of butter
1 onion
1/2 leek
1 clove of garlic
1 carrot
1 small parsley
3 potatoes
1 and 1/2 liters of broth (poultry or vegetable)
1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder
400 g green or yellow green beans (frozen out of season)
1 tablespoon of chopped dill
200 g of 18% cream or 80 ml of 18% cream from a carton (for soups and sauces)
PREPARATION
Sauté the diced onion in olive oil and butter in a pot. Rinse the leek, peel off the thicker outer layers and cut off the green ends. Cut the remaining white and light green parts lengthwise into 4 parts, rinse them and cut them into slices.
Add to the pot with the onion and fry for about 2 minutes. At the end, add the pressed garlic.
Add peeled and thinly sliced ​​carrots and parsley and mix. Peel the potatoes and cut into cubes. Add to the pot and stir-fry for about 2 minutes.
Pour in the hot broth, season with salt and pepper, add turmeric and bring to a boil. Cover and cook for approx. 15 minutes. Halfway throug

cooking, add the green beans, rinsed in a strainer (and thawed if using frozen).
Remove from heat and add chopped dill and cream (thick cream from a cup should be tempered with a few spoons of soup, while sweet cream from a carton can be poured directly into the soup).
Enjoy your meal
[End]

metadata.prompt:
Ingredients:

4 medium-sized potatoes, peeled and cut into thick fries/chips
Vegetable oil for frying
4 white fish fillets (such as cod, haddock or plaice)
1 cup all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon salt
1 cup cold sparkling water or beer
Salt and malt vinegar, to serve
Instructions:

Prepare the chips: Cut the potatoes into thick, even-sized chips. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes to remove some of the starch. Drain well and pat dry with paper towels.

Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy bottomed pan to 320°F (160°C). Fry the chips in batches for 5-7 minutes until light golden. Drain on paper towels.

Make the batter: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt. Slowly whisk in the cold sparkling water or beer to make a smooth, lump-free batter.

Pat the fish fillets dry and season with salt. Dip the fish into the batter, coating all sides.

Increase the oil temperature to 350°F (180°C). Carefully add the battered fish to the hot oil and fry for 3-5 minutes until golden brown and crispy.

Drain the fried fish and chips on paper towels. Season with additional salt.

Serve the fish and chips hot, with malt vinegar and lemon wedges on the side.

meta.prompt:
Song Description for AI Music Generation
Song Title: Lyrical Ascent

Overall Vibe & Mood: The track should feel like a struggle and a climb. It begins with a dark, introspective, and almost claustrophobic mood, then gradually builds in intensity, anger, and defiance, culminating in an explosive and triumphant climax. The overall tone is gritty, cinematic, and deeply personal.

Target BPM: 92 BPM

Part 1: The Beat / Instrumentation
Intro (0:00 - 0:15): Start with a simple, melancholic piano loop in a minor key (like C minor). The piano should sound slightly detuned or like an old upright. Layer this with the sound of a pencil scratching furiously on paper and a faint, distant sound of rainfall.

Verse 1 (0:15 - 0:48): The piano loop continues. Introduce a classic, hard-hitting boom-bap drum pattern. The kick drum should be deep and heavy, and the snare should have a sharp, cracking sound. A deep, subtle sub-bass line enters, playing a simple root note pattern that follows the piano chords.

Pre-Chorus (0:48 - 1:04): The drums simplify to just a kick and a hi-hat pattern. Introduce tense, rising string pads (violins, cellos) in the background to build anticipation.

Chorus (1:04 - 1:36): The beat becomes anthemic. The drums hit harder, with an open hi-hat on the off-beats. The piano is now layered with a distorted electric guitar riff that mirrors the main melody. The strings swell to become more prominent and dramatic.

Verse 2 (1:36 - 2:08): The beat returns to the boom-bap style of Verse 1, but this time with a more aggressive and constant hi-hat pattern to drive the energy. The pencil scratching sound returns faintly.

Chorus (2:08 - 2:40): Same as the first chorus, but perhaps with an added layer of ad-lib vocalizations in the background (e.g., "Yeah!", "Let's go!").

Bridge (2:40 - 3:12): A major shift. The drums and bass drop out completely. Only the haunting piano loop and the rising, tense strings remain. The rainfall sound effect becomes more prominent. This creates a moment of vulnerability and reflection before the final explosion.

Verse 3 / Climax (3:12 - 3:58): The beat crashes back in, faster and more frantic. Implement double-time hi-hats (16th notes). The sub-bass is now a more complex, driving line. A subtle, distorted synth arp is added in the background to create a feeling of chaos and urgency.

Outro (3:58 - 4:15): The beat abruptly cuts out. All that's left is the final chord of the piano ringing out, the sound of the pencil dropping on a table, followed by a single, deep, exhausted breath. Fade to silence.

Part 2: Vocal Flow & Lyrical Content
The vocal delivery should be dynamic, mirroring the emotional arc of the song. The rapper's voice should go from a controlled, introspective mumble to a strained, aggressive shout.

Flow Style: Eminem circa 2002-2010. Heavy focus on multi-syllabic rhyme schemes, complex internal rhymes, and rhythmic variation. The flow should often feel slightly ahead of or behind the beat (syncopation).

Lyrical Theme: The song is a metaphor for overcoming creative struggle and self-doubt by mastering the art of lyricism. The "ascent" is the climb out of writer's block and mediocrity to a peak of verbal dexterity.

Structure Breakdown:
Intro (Spoken Word, low intensity):

Content: The rapper is talking to himself, staring at a blank page.

Example Bars: "This pen feels like a brick... page is too white, the room is too quiet. Gotta climb outta this. One word at a time."

Verse 1 (Building Intensity):

Flow: Starts slow and deliberate, almost conversational. As the verse progresses, the pace quickens, and more complex rhyme chains are introduced.

Content: Describes the feeling of being trapped by self-doubt and the pressure to create. Uses metaphors of suffocation and being lost.

Rhyme Style Example: "Stuck in a lyrical paralysis, this is a fatal analysis / My mind's a broken abacus, can't calculate a path past this / The doubt's a heavy catalyst..."

Chorus (Anthemic, Powerful Delivery):

Flow: Slower, more rhythmic, and percussive. Each word should land with the beat for maximum impact. A very catchy, repeatable cadence.

Content: The core thesis. This isn't just music; it's a fight for survival and sanity.

Example Bars: "This ain't a track, it's a panic attack on a wax slab! / This ain't a rhyme, it's a vertical climb, can't turn back! / This ain't a song, this is where I belong, up in the clouds! / This is my Lyrical Ascent, screaming it out loud!"

Verse 2 (Aggressive, Confrontational):

Flow: Faster, more staccato, and angrier. The rapper is pushing against the beat, creating a feeling of tension.

Content: The target shifts from internal doubt to external critics and the state of the rap game. He's sharpening his words into weapons.

Rhyme Style Example: "So I'm stackin' up syllables, turnin' 'em into military drills / They're barely digestible, for all you rappers with minimal skills / I'm predictably volatile, you're just a decimal point on my bills..."

Bridge (Vulnerable, Breathy Delivery):

Flow: Slows down dramatically. The delivery is almost a whisper, filled with emotion. Lines are shorter, with more space between them.

Content: A moment of quiet reflection. Why go through this struggle? The answer is that it's the only thing that makes him feel alive.

Example Bars: "And for a second I ask why... / Why bleed on the page? Why scream at the sky? / ...'Cause the silence... is a slower way to die."

Verse 3 (Explosive, "Rap God" Climax):

Flow: A technical showcase. Near-breathless, rapid-fire, multi-syllabic onslaught. The rhyme schemes become incredibly dense and complex.

Content: The rapper has reached the "summit." The lyrics are pure braggadocio about his lyrical skill, using imagery of climbing, flying, and god-like power. It's a pure display of technical mastery.

Rhyme Style Example: "I'm a verbal phenomenon, droppin' a comet on top of the Parthenon! / What are you stoppin' me for? I'm an unstoppable force, you're an oxymoron! / The acrobatics of phonics, I'm past supersonic, you're comically chronic..."

Outro (Spoken Word, Exhausted):

Content: Just a single, final thought after the storm.

Example Bar: "...Okay. ...Next page."
